shared_elements: concentric circles / disc motif (rosette-like discs in A's band, concentric rings in B)
horizontal band or line spanning the surface
radiating spoke-like lines (chariot wheel spokes vs. rays around the disc)
justification: Both surfaces show a human-like figure and circular/radiating disc motifs set against horizontal dividing bands, but these are generic forms found almost anywhere: A's discs are small repeated rosettes in a border and spoked wheels, while B's is a large rayed concentric disc fused to the body of a single figure. A depicts a detailed narrative procession of naturalistically modelled robed men, a horse and chariot in profile with careful anatomy and drapery, whereas B is a single, extremely schematic stick-limbed figure in outline with no scene, so the manner of depiction and the content are fundamentally unrelated.
